news.title: ‘Full support’ for Infantino: Six Arab federations defy growing revolt over World Cup plan
news.lede: Six Arab football federations have thrown their weight behind Gianni Infantino, declaring their “full support” for the embattled FIFA president as opposition to his controversial World Cup investment plan continues to grow.The backing came from Morocco, Qatar, Egypt, Mauritania, Lebanon and Sudan on Thursday, with four of the six federation chiefs also serving on the FIFA Council. Their public show of support comes days after Infantino withdrew a proposed USD 20 billion private investment plan linked to the World Cup following a fierce backlash from football officials around the world.“. news.title: Referee Yiembe: From dusty fields of Nakuru, to Fifa Club World Cup and Uefa Super Cup
news.lede: Aston Villa's John McGinn remonstrates to assistant referee Stephen Yiembe during UEFA Super Cup final on Wednesday. Assistant referee Stephen Yiembe from Kenya boasts an impressive medal haul from officiating at major sporting championships across the globe. But Yembe’s story can’t be told without stating one caveat: Fifa does not allow referees to grant interviews to the media without clearance from the headquarters in Zurich. The latest addition to Yiembe’s medal collection is undoubtedly one of his most prestigious - the medal he received on Wednesday night after officiating the 2026 Uefa Super Cup final as one of two assistant referees.

news.title: NZ Football pulls support for Infantino as FIFA President
news.lede: New Zealand Football has pulled its support for Gianni Infantino as FIFA President amid the fallout from the embattled executive's failed World Cup sell-off plan. NZ Football, which governs the game in Aotearoa, also called for an independent review of the steps taken during the plan's development. "After careful consideration, NZF has formed the view that decisions and actions within FIFA have contributed to a breakdown in trust and increased division within international football, and that an independent review is required to restore confidence and trust," it said in a statement. "NZF believes this point in time represents an opportunity for all FIFA member associations to advocate for stronger governance, accountability and transparency which are fundamental in maintaining confidence of the administration of the global game."

news.title: New Zealand Football withdraws support for Infantino, urges review
news.lede: Gianni Infantino came under renewed fire this week after three confederations signed an open letter accusing the world football boss of breaking trust 'through deception'. (EPA Images pic) WELLINGTON: New Zealand Football said on Friday it had withdrawn support for Fifa boss Gianni Infantino and called for an independent review into his aborted plan to sell off part of the World Cup. Infantino came under renewed fire this week in an open letter signed by three confederations – Uefa, North and Central America's CONCACAF and Asia's AFC – accusing the world football boss of breaking trust "through deception". It is believed they want the Swiss official to resign before he has the chance to seek re-election in March next year.

news.title: Norway's Viking Row took over the World Cup — here's how the viral fan tradition began
news.lede: Norway did not win the 2026 FIFA World Cup. But it may have created the tournament's most enduring tradition. During the tournament, thousands of fans sat on streets, in stadiums and even inside subway cars, pulling imaginary oars in perfect unison while shouting "Ro!" Videos spread from Oslo to Times Square, airport terminals, fighter jets, beaches and eventually the World Cup champions' own victory celebration.

news.title: Banyana end Falcons’ World Cup hopes
news.lede: Super Falcons’ hopes of qualifying for the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil ended on Thursday after they lost 2-1 to South Africa in the Confederation of African Football play-off match at the 2026 WAFCON in Morocco, PUNCH Sports Extra reports. The Falcons had missed out on an automatic World Cup ticket after their quarter-final defeat by Cameroon on Sunday. The defeat to Cameroon also ended Nigeria’s run of reaching at least the semi-finals at every previous edition of the WAFCON and handed the 10-time African champions their worst-ever finish in the competition. However, Nigeria had another opportunity to revive their hopes of maintaining their record of featuring at every edition of the FIFA Women’s World Cup, but the Falcons were unable to overcome South Africa.

news.title: Bayern Munich president Herbert Hainer relieved FIFA’s privatization plan is dead
news.lede: Bayern Munich president Herbert Hainer expressed his relief over the scrapping of FIFA’s recent proposal to sell the rights to the men’s and women’s World Cups and Club World Cups to private investors. FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced on Tuesday a plan with private investors to create a $20 billion company which would be in charge of running major football tournaments. The idea was met with immediate backlash from governing bodies like UEFA and CONCACAF and eventually cancelled. In an interview with Abendzeitung, Hainer expressed his relief over the dismissal of the initiative.
